claims.value: Five cameras and two participants were studied with OpenPose at 1920x1080/120 Hz and 3840x2160/30 Hz for walking, jumping and throwing.
claims.limitations: Rate and resolution changed together. Observed task/keypoint errors do not isolate the effect of frame rate or qualify an industrial camera or golf-swing endpoint.

claims.value: OpenCap collected 720x1280 smartphone video at 60 Hz and aligned keypoint trajectories using cross-correlations of keypoint velocities.
claims.limitations: Software temporal alignment is not hardware exposure synchronization. Model-based dynamics and the tested tasks do not transfer accuracy to golf or this proposed rig.

claims.value: Ten participants performed eight movements; the abstract reports larger hip differences, especially during rapid movements such as running.
claims.limitations: Abstract rechecked through Europe PMC metadata; full-text retrieval unavailable during this review. Marker-based agreement is not absolute truth, and these results do not qualify any proposed camera or establish universal speed-dependent error.

claims.value: Evaluate two matched global-shutter color cameras at 120 frames per second or faster with common hardware triggering before purchasing a full rig.

recommendations.task: Fast whole-body and implement-adjacent shop motion with an eventual six-to-eight-camera volume.
qualification_gates: Obtain complete comparable quotes and exact SDK EULAs.
Measure two-camera exposure skew, drops, jitter, and sustained full-rate payload.
Measure pose and triangulation error throughout the intended volume under shop lighting and occlusion.
Verify lens field of view, working distance, focus lock, exposure, blur, and lighting safety.
Scale the proven topology to six and eight cameras without sharing an unqualified USB bottleneck.
recommendations.decision: Define the output error budget and obtain quotes first. Select a matched pilot pair only after mode, lens, timing, software and host review; compare FLIR temporal sampling with Basler default-region resolution at 164 fps using measured results.
recommendations.limitations: This is an engineering-screen recommendation, not procurement approval or a claim of biomechanical accuracy.

recommendations.task: Distributed eight-camera reference-rig evaluation across large room spans using 5GigE/2.5GigE transport and IEEE 1588 PTP synchronization.
qualification_gates: Benchmark 8-camera distributed Ethernet topology with mode-sized switches and NICs.
Measure exposure midpoint skew with the selected clock/trigger architecture and packet jitter separately under sustained network load.
Confirm the selected SDK/transport integration and benchmark each supported producer or adapter in isolation without coupling to open core.
Verify sustained 8-camera write throughput and thermal stability in the capture space.
Obtain formal multi-camera enterprise quotes including C-mount optics, qualified cabling, and PoE infrastructure.
recommendations.decision: Distinguish the two-camera USB pilot from the distributed eight-camera reference-rig evaluation. A successful USB pilot does not establish an eight-camera distributed topology; evaluate Allied Vision Alvium G5-203 and LUCID Triton2 TRT016S-CC as dedicated Ethernet/PTP candidates for the full lab.
recommendations.limitations: Provisional architecture evaluation only; no multi-camera Ethernet throughput, PTP skew, or pose accuracy test has been executed.

recommendations.task: Larger or cable-constrained capture volume where rugged synchronized GMSL2 links are more important than full-resolution sampling above 60 fps.
qualification_gates: Confirm the exact full-resolution frame rate required by every intended task.
Benchmark the complete capture-card and NVIDIA compute topology with the intended camera count.
Review proprietary SDK, driver, model, redistribution, and hardware lock-in terms.
Measure pose accuracy against the fast-motion pilot rather than assuming depth or vendor synchronization improves it.
recommendations.decision: Keep the ZED X One GS as a topology evaluation, not the default fast-motion purchase. Its synchronized GMSL2 architecture is attractive for long cable runs, but full-resolution video is limited to 60 fps and the stack adds capture-card, NVIDIA, fixed-lens, and proprietary-SDK constraints.
recommendations.limitations: No physical comparison, price-normalized quote, or open-core adapter has been completed.
